transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CSM) — Maya Patel (Stellar Insights), Luis Ortega (Platform Lead), Sofia Ruiz (DevOps), Ben Walker (Product)

Summary (auto): Quarterly business review focused on health, cost, reliability, and next steps for pilot/renewal.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Alex from Redwood. With me is Priya and Jordan. How are we doing over at Stellar?
[00:08] Maya (Stellar): Good, thanks. Busy end of quarter but wanted to make sure we got this QBR on the calendar.
[00:13] Alex: Great. Agenda, quick usage and cost overview, reliability incidents, then roadmap and security questions, and finish with next steps. Sound good?
[00:21] Luis (Stellar): Yep, that works.
[00:24] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll kick off with the metrics slide — apologies if transcription picks up the slide as "metrics light" again —
[00:30] Priya: So, usage trend: tokens per day have grown ~28% q/q, embeddings stable, most of the load is conversational API. We're seeing tail latency creeping up during peak times.
[00:42] Maya: Right, we noticed more 95th percentile spikes the last two weeks; it's causing occasional page timeouts for support agents.
[00:49] Priya: Exactly. On hosted we've observed queuing at the inference layer; that's where Dedicated helps by reserving GPU pools and predictable throughput. Also we recommended KV cache tuning, we saw a miss-rate on the prefix cache that increases effective token cost.
[01:05] Luis: When you say KV cache, do you mean the "KV cash" you mentioned earlier in the doc? I think ops misconstrued that as an external cache.
[01:12] Priya: Yeah, sorry — KV cache as in key-value attention cache in the model runtime. It's internal but configuration impacts latency.
[01:19] Ben (Stellar): Can you quantify cost delta if we move to Dedicated? Our CFO asks, is it cheaper or just more predictable?
[01:26] Alex: Good question. Short answer: dedicated is typically higher base cost because you're reserving capacity, but unit cost per token often goes down for heavy steady workloads due to batching and predictable kernel selection. We also have committed discount tiers. We'll send modelled comparisons.
[01:39] Maya: Our monthly spend has jumped 42% this quarter; we need to understand leak or just growth.
[01:45] Jordan (CSM): From health checks we saw elevated inference retries and a few fallback events where requests were routed to a smaller model variant which increased token usage.
[01:54] Sofia (Stellar): Those fallbacks — were they due to capacity or policy?
[01:58] Priya: Mostly capacity and autoscale thresholds. There were two incidents last month during peak ingest where fallback policy routed to a smaller variant. We flagged those and changed the routing thresholds mid-month.
[02:08] Sofia: Any logs we can look at? Our SRE wants traces.
[02:11] Priya: Yes, please share staging logs; we can annotate. Action item for Sofia to provide access.
[02:16] Luis: On reliability, we had one day where SLA hit 97.6%; we need to get back above 99.5.
[02:23] Alex: Understood — Dedicated plus conservative routing policies should improve that. Also cross-region failover can help, but that adds egress and multi-region complexity.
[02:34] Ben: Security question — we handle sensitive PII in prompts. Are there any new SOC 2 / KMS integrations we should be aware of?
[02:42] Jordan: We're SOC 2 audited. For Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed key rotation. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and logs with redaction options.
[02:53] Maya: We might need a VPC option for certain data flows; is that available?
[02:57] Alex: Yes, Redwood Private offers VPC and on-prem options. We'll share the security pack and network diagram.
[03:05] Sofia: Good. One more — model upgrades. We saw a small regression after last model bump in January; how do you handle rollbacks?
[03:12] Priya: We do canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. We also keep evals tied to prompt sets. In your case, we identified a distribution shift in prompts causing a quality regression and we pinned the model for the affected routes.
[03:25] Maya: Nice.
[03:27] Priya: For the benchmarks, I'll run the 95th percentile latency tests on a Dedicated cluster (same config you were looking at) and share the spreadsheet. That will show steady-state p95 and cost per million tokens estimates.
[03:38] Maya: Awesome — that's exactly what we need to present to finance.
[03:41] Alex: On pricing, we'll provide two options — committed capacity (monthly reserved) and hybrid burst (reserved plus burst-on-demand). We'll include net unit economics in both.
[03:51] Ben: Do you have anything that compares Redwood to Anthropic/OpenAI in our specific workload?
[03:56] Priya: We have a benchmark pack; we'll highlight latency and cost for your prompt mix. Note that external model providers often differ on pricing granularity.
[04:05] Luis: Any blockers on our side?
[04:07] Sofia: We'll need to share staging logs and grant an S3 role to Redwood for trace access; security already approved a scoped role.
[04:14] Jordan: Thanks Sofia — we'll take that as an action item.
[04:18] Alex: Quick recap of next steps: Priya runs benchmarks (due 04/03), Alex sends pricing (due 04/07), Jordan schedules pilot review (week of 04/13), Sofia to provide logs (due 03/31). Anything else?
[04:31] Maya: Can you also include an example config for KV cache tuning? Our ML team wants that.
[04:34] Priya: Yes, we'll include recommended cache TTLs and prefix strategies; full config in the benchmark doc.
[04:41] Ben: Also want to confirm any impact to tokens from fallback routing — can you include examples in the spreadsheet?
[04:47] Priya: Yep, we'll show before/after token counts for the fallback incidents.
[04:52] Alex: Perfect. Thank you all — we'll follow up over email.
[04:56] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[04:58] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" vs KV cache, product names like "Redwood Dedicated" transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate").
